headline: GOLD BREAKS $4,000 SUPPORT, CRASHES TO $3,897; SILVER SMASHES THROUGH $50 AS FED HIKE BETS SPIKE
snippet: Gold tumbled 3.1% to US$3,897/oz on Friday — its lowest level since early September — decisively breaking the $4,000 support cited by analysts as the key line in the sand. Silver was dragged below $50/oz for the first time in several months, amplifying gold's losses. Stronger-than-expected US jobs and manufacturing data deepened market bets on a December Fed rate hike, strengthening the dollar and driving Treasury yields higher. Gold has now fallen roughly 26% from its January 2026 all-time high above $5,300.

headline: KINROSS Q3: MARGINS SURGE 19% TO $2,747/OZ BUT VOLUME DOWN 20%; FIRST GOLD POURED AT REDBIRD
snippet: Kinross Gold (TSX: K / NYSE: KGC) reported Q3 2026 earnings of $583 million ($0.49/share) on revenue of US$1,775 million, with gold-equivalent ounce sales down 20% year-on-year to 417,657 oz due to portfolio changes and lower-grade quarters at key mines. The bright spots: operating margins improved 19% to US$2,747/oz, the company poured first gold at its new Redbird project, and free cash flow came in at US$391 million adjusted. Kinross also raised its capital return target to 50% of adjusted FCF after buying back 5% of shares since April 2025.

headline: ALAMOS Q3: ISLAND GOLD SHAFT SLIPS TO MID-2027; AISC HITS $1,956/OZ AS 119K OZ MEETS GUIDANCE
snippet: Alamos Gold (TSX/NYSE: AGI) produced 119,000 oz in Q3 2026 at all-in sustaining costs of US$1,956/oz — meeting quarterly guidance, but with adjusted EPS of $0.44 falling short of consensus on revenue of $510 million. A key negative: the Island Gold mine's production shaft has been delayed approximately one quarter to mid-2027, trimming near-term production growth. Full-year guidance of 510,000–560,000 oz remains intact, with heavier output weighted to Q4.

headline: NORTHWEST COPPER EXPANDS KWANIKA WESTERN ZONE AT DEPTH: 73.9m AT 1.39% CuEq FROM 457m
snippet: NorthWest Copper (TSXV: NWST) intersected 73.9 metres at 1.39% copper-equivalent (0.51% Cu, 0.79 g/t Au) from 457 metres depth in the latest holes from its 2026 Kwanika drill program in British Columbia, extending the Western Zone at depth. Assays are now back from 17 of 43 holes drilled in the 2026 program, with the Western Zone continuing to show broad, consistent copper-gold porphyry mineralisation that remains open to depth and to the northwest.

headline: BLOSSOM GOLD HITS 128m AT 1.19 g/t GOLD INCLUDING 37m AT 2.82 g/t AT NEVADA'S ROSEBUD PROJECT
snippet: Blossom Gold reported a 128-metre intersection at 1.19 g/t gold — including a 37.1-metre high-grade core at 2.82 g/t — from surface drilling at its Rosebud Project in Nevada. The broad, shallow intersection supports potential for a bulk-tonnage open-pit style deposit in one of the world's top-ranked mining jurisdictions. The result adds to the growing drill database at Rosebud and defines mineralisation from surface, a key economic advantage at any gold price.

headline: MYRIAD URANIUM DRILLS 34m AT 399 PPM eU3O8 IN PHASE II AT COPPER MOUNTAIN, WYOMING
snippet: Myriad Uranium (TSXV: MYRM) released further Phase II drill results from its Copper Mountain Project in Wyoming's Powder River Basin, with the best hole intersecting 34.29 metres at 399 ppm eU3O8 across five boreholes. The results confirm wide, roll-front style uranium mineralisation characteristic of Wyoming's licensed ISR uranium districts. Myriad is advancing toward a resource estimate as the global uranium long-term contract price holds above US$96/lb — above the 2007 peak.

headline: CRITICAL METALS + EUROPEAN LITHIUM COMBINATION COMPLETE — WOLFSBERG + TANBREEZ MERGED; NASDAQ LISTING BEGINS NOV 6
snippet: Critical Metals Corp. (Nasdaq: CRML) completed its acquisition of European Lithium on October 27 after the Australian court approved schemes of arrangement and securityholders voted in favour. New shares issued to European Lithium shareholders will begin trading on Nasdaq on November 6. The combined entity holds the Wolfsberg hard-rock lithium project in Austria — one of Europe's most advanced lithium developments — alongside Critical Metals' Tanbreez rare earth project in Greenland, creating a European-Greenlandic critical minerals developer.

headline: OCTOBER CLOBBERS PRECIOUS METALS 7% — OANDA: RATE CYCLE IS A PAUSE, NOT A STRUCTURAL RESET
snippet: OANDA's October 2026 precious metals wrap shows gold down roughly 7% during the month — from $4,182 to the current $3,897 level — as the Fed's return to rate hikes crushes near-term sentiment. But OANDA argues the structural long-term bull case is intact: central bank buying continues at record pace, de-dollarisation trends are entrenched, and real rates remain historically low relative to inflation. OANDA identifies $3,800 as the critical technical support for the next directional signal, and notes that every prior Fed rate cycle since 2008 has eventually given way to further easing.

headline: GOLD/SILVER RATIO TESTS 75 AS SILVER ERASES SPRING GAINS — FED HAWKS PUNISH INDUSTRIAL-MONETARY HYBRID
snippet: ISA Bullion's October 27 daily analysis flagged silver trading just below $53 with the gold/silver ratio at 75 — before Friday's further collapse took silver through $50. Futures markets were pricing over 80% odds of a December Fed hike, and Chinese industrial demand remains muted. Silver's dual monetary-industrial character makes it more exposed than gold to rate cycles: in prior Fed hike episodes (2015–2018, 2022–2023) the ratio spiked past 80 before recovering sharply once the cycle peaked. Current levels have historically marked high-conviction entry points for patient silver accumulators.

headline: 5 CANADIAN GOLD MINERS TO WATCH IN NOVEMBER — ISLAND GOLD, DETOUR LAKE, MALARTIC LEAD SCREENS
snippet: Canadian Mining Report identifies five Canadian gold producers trading near multi-year discounts to spot NAV as Q3 reporting season wraps, with Agnico Eagle, Barrick, Kinross, IAMGOLD and Alamos all reporting within the October 28 to November 9 window. The piece notes that energy costs — Brent crude running at US$116/barrel — remain a live headwind for every mine on the list, keeping AISC elevated even as gold prices corrected. The analysts argue the best-positioned names are those with low-energy-intensity underground operations such as Island Gold and Detour Lake's truck-trolley-assisted haul.
